bpn.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.

ip.context: A drip irrigation emitter (dripper/micro-sprinkler) that delivers water at a controlled low flow rate directly to the soil or plant root zone. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.

Ukrainian: 'крапельниця' is the field term used by irrigation workers. zh CORRECTED (2026-07-10, category-4 wave-2 QA): the wave-2 zh translating agent initially deviated to the generic academic term '灌水器' throughout ip_ keys, reasoning that the calculator's emitter-exponent model (x from ~0 to 0.5) is generic rather than drip-only. ip.context: Ratio of minimum to average emitter flow rate in a drip or sprinkler system. DU = q_min / q_avg. Appears in Drip/Sprinkler calculator.

When the source says 'low-quarter DU', see the separate 'low-quarter distribution uniformity' entry. Hebrew: אחידות — never the nonword הוודות (found in shipped he file). mhp.context: Total elevation difference between the headpond water surface and the turbine — before subtracting penstock losses. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Gross' means total/before-deduction. Pair with 'net head' for clarity. Use the hydro-power standard term.

mhp.context: Effective head available at the turbine after subtracting penstock friction and minor losses from gross head. H_net = H_gross - h_L.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Net' means after-deduction. Pair with 'gross head'. Use the hydro-power standard term. WMO No. 385 entry 111 ('available head') gives the Russian term 'полезный напор' (useful head) / syn. 'располагаемый напор' — these overlap with net head in Russian hydro engineering practice.

mhp.context: Overall efficiency of a micro-hydro power plant — product of turbine, generator, and transmission efficiencies. Dimensionless, 0–1. Appears in Micro-Hydro Power calculator.
mhp.translation_notes: 'Plant' here means the power plant/installation, not a living plant. mi.context: Dimensionless ratio of vertical drop to horizontal distance (rise/run). Used as channel slope (S_0) and friction slope in Manning and Darcy-Weisbach calculators. English aliases 'slope' and 'grade' (u_grade/u_gradePercent) both point here.
mi.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 477 ('energy gradient') confirms Russian: 'энергетический уклон' (energy slope) — the base term 'уклон' is WMO-verified. In open-channel hydraulics, 'slope' is the energy gradient — not a geometric angle. Use the civil engineering term for gradient/grade, not a geographic or topographic term. [2026-07-21] Centralized the grade activity-sense guard here (was living only as u_grade/u_gradePercent label commentary): the 'avoid' array now carries the running/walking/jogging exercise-incline trap, so the slope entry is the single home for the grade→energy-gradient concept and its wrong senses.

mi.context: A channel whose cross-section is non-uniform / non-prismatic — a natural or surveyed section defined by station-elevation points, as opposed to a regular trapezoidal shape. Titles the Manning Irregular Channel calculator (mi_) and, in the geometric sense, the Weir Flow Irregular calculator (wi_).
mi.translation_notes: "Irregular" here is GEOMETRIC: the cross-section is non-uniform / natural / arbitrary shape. It is NOT the temporal sense "sporadic / occasional / not-regular" (bg "нередовен" WRONG, uk "нерегулярний" WRONG per Bulgarian-engineer-feedback.md), and NOT "incorrect / faulty" (ru "неправильное русло" reads as "wrong channel" — prefer "произвольного сечения"). Where the language allows, name the cross-section explicitly ("of irregular cross-section") rather than a bare adjective that could be read as temporal or evaluative. Task 98 audit (2026-07-13): uk/ru were already fixed to the geometric sense, but bg was still shipping the evaluative-sense defect this note itself warns against — "неправилно сечение" (= "incorrect/wrong cross-section"), across 7 occurrences (mi_menu, mi_main_title, mi_main_desc, wi_menu, wi_main_title, wi_main_desc, irr_card_canal_desc). Fixed to "произволно сечение" ("arbitrary cross-section"), a direct grammatical parallel to the Russian fix. Lesson: a documented glossary warning doesn't guarantee every flagged language was actually corrected — verify current shipped state, don't assume a note describes present reality.

ws.context: A flow-measurement or water-control structure — a barrier across a channel over which water flows. Appears in Weir Flow Simple and Weir Flow Irregular calculators.
ws.translation_notes: WMO No. 385 entry 1665 confirms: es = 'vertedero', fr = 'déversoir', ru = 'водослив'. In an irrigation context, the term often overlaps with 'diversion dam' or 'check structure'. Use the term most common among irrigation field workers in the target language, not a purely civil-engineering dictionary term.

ws.context: Hydraulic head — energy per unit weight of water, expressed as a height of water column. The ROOT concept behind head loss, velocity head, weir head, and gross/net head. A length, never a pressure. Appears as a bare label in Weir Flow (ws_headWaterHeight), Orifice (or_head), and Manning Pipe Flow (mpf_velocity_head). Acceptable English synonyms (translate the concept, not the exact word): energy elevation, hydraulic grade line (HGL).
ws.translation_notes: Newly seeded 2026-07-20 to close the long-standing gap where only the COMPOUNDS (head loss, velocity/weir/gross/net head) had entries but the root word 'head' did not — the root is what every agent re-derived (and sometimes mistranslated as anatomical head or pressure). Values below are the roots extracted from those compound entries and are best-effort/derived, not natively verified — confirm in the term-centric sweep (see ROADMAP). Several languages split the root by sense: the hydro-power 'fall' sense uses a different word than the pipe 'head' sense (cs spád vs tlaková výška; hr/sr visina·pad vs visina; ro sarcină vs cădere; tr yük vs düşü; ar علو/الارتفاع vs الضغط). Where that split exists, keep the pipe/energy-head root here and let the fall-sense compounds keep their own word. Slavic напор/напір, sw kimo (corrected from kichwa — see 2026-07-22 note below), and the هد/ہیډ/ہیڈ/हेड/ሄድ loanword family are consistent and documented across the suite (see 'head loss' notes). [2026-07-21 Task 128 RESOLVED — Tom decision] Native review is not realistically available for these; rely on AI guidance and defer to the locally natural term. Anatomically-derived head words are NOT inherently wrong (English 'head' is itself anatomical) — a blanket anatomical-head avoid was mistaken and has been reframed above. Accordingly: my or_head/ws_headWaterHeight 'ခေါင်းဆုံး' (contains ခေါင်း) is KEPT as a locally natural term — NOT a defect; the earlier ဖိမြင့်ဆင့် root is one acceptable variant, ခေါင်းဆုံး is another, both stand. he or_head/ws_headWaterHeight 'עומק' (depth) is KEPT as-is — for orifice effective head a depth-to-centroid reading is physically legitimate, and it is a natural term. This does NOT license reverting the documented cs/he/sw velocity-head calque fixes (rychlostní výška, עומד מהירות, kimo cha kasi): those were replaced because the anatomical word was not the natural term there, which the reframed avoid guard still forbids. hi: or_head uses शीर्ष, velocity-head same शीर्ष, root here is the हेड loanword — harmless internal variance, polish only. [2026-07-21 Task 131 tip sprint] Definitional tips now ship in all 26 languages on or_head/ws_headWaterHeight/mpf_velocity_head ('energy per unit weight of water, a height of water column, not a pressure' / 'kinetic energy as a height of water column'), anchoring the concept at point-of-use. am head re-verified CLEAN this pass: uses the ሄድ loanword, no ጭንቅ (distress) calque anywhere. my (ခေါင်းဆုံး) and he (עומק) or_head/ws labels CLOSED 2026-07-21 as locally natural (see Task 128 resolution above) — no label change made. Task 130 (2026-07-21): am odt_ keys (odt_h1, odt_notes_1_def) still carried the ጭንቅ (distress) calque for head, missed by earlier sweeps; fixed to ሄድ. [2026-07-22 sw head family → kimo, Tom + Kenya-engineer input] REVERSES 'sw kichwa': kichwa (body-part head) is NOT the Swahili engineering term for hydraulic head. Anchor — velocity head was already 'kimo cha kasi' (the accepted descriptive term), so kimo is the register's word for head and kichwa was a body-part calque. Applied across the sw lang file (mhp_gross_head, mhp_hl_check, mhp_notes_3_def, rc_notes_7_def, odt_notes_1_def, or_head + ws_headWaterHeight labels): head=kimo cha maji, head loss=upotevu wa kimo, gross=kimo cha jumla cha maji, net=kimo halisi cha maji, weir head=kimo cha maji juu ya kizingiti. Ride-alongs same pass: crown taji(royal)→kilele (or_ orifice crown; rc_ crest already kilele); weir kizuizi/bwawa→kizingiti cha maji ('water sill', incl. ws_/wi_ calculator identities, Lenye→Chenye noun-class agreement); specific gravity uzito maalum KEPT. RATIONALE: for the 0.65 low-resource languages engineering discourse happens in English (TZ/KE engineering education is English-medium); the local tongue lives at the field/extension register, so there is no fixed engineering-Swahili standard to defer to — descriptive clarity for a Swahili-speaking field worker is the goal, and TANZANIA is the specific target audience (Tom's Kenya engineer). See memory project_low_resource_register_reality. [2026-07-27 sw kichwa->kimo COMPLETED, ROADMAP Task 147] The 2026-07-22 decision above was only applied to the seven keys it named, leaving lib/lang.ec.sw.php split almost in half: 15 keys on kimo, 16 still on kichwa -- including the identity strings (menu + <title> + desc) of ALL THREE head-loss calculators (dw_, hw_, mphl_), which is the first thing a Swahili speaker saw. Found while closing Task 141. All 16 now converted: dw_/hw_/mphl_ main_menu+main_title+main_desc, mhp_hnet, mhp_notes_1_term, mhp_notes_1_def, mhp_notes_3_term, odt_h1, rc_Hp, ip_max_head. Head loss = 'Upotevu wa Kimo' (Title Case in identity strings, lowercase in prose, matching mhp_hl_check); net head = 'Kimo halisi' (parallel to mhp_gross_head 'Kimo cha jumla'). template_printable_title/_subtitle KEPT as Kichwa -- there it means 'title/heading', not the hydraulic sense. The swap was safe as a straight word substitution because kichwa and kimo are both noun class 7, so every cha/wa/kinacho- concord marker stayed valid. Verified: php -l clean, tag parity vs English on all 16, and back-translation of each. rc_Hp keeps 'bwawa' for weir (consistent with its already-converted sibling rc_notes_7_def); the ws_/wi_ kizingiti standardization is a separate concern. LESSON: a terminology decision recorded here is not applied until someone greps the whole file -- the 2026-07-22 note listed the keys it changed, which read as completion but was a partial pass.

keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_1_def: Solves one set of demands at a time, using the same gradient method EPANET uses. It does not model how the network changes over time.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_2_def: Tanks, water quality, and control valves that open and close on their own (PRV, PSV, FCV) are not modeled. A pipe can carry a fixed minor loss, but not a valve whose open or closed state depends on the flow being solved for.
keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_3_def: Every project is a tab, and every tab is saved in this browser as you work. Clearing your browser data deletes them all, so keep your work in a file: File, Save as. An asterisk on a tab means it holds changes that are not in a file. Nothing is ever written to a file unless you ask. keys_to_translate.lpn_notes_5_def: A pump follows H = H₀ − aQ^b, where H is the head the pump adds and Q is the flow through it. Enter one, two, or three points from the manufacturer's curve. Three points — the head at zero flow, the normal working point, and the point of highest flow — fit H₀, a and b directly, and follow a published curve most closely. Two points fit a parabola (b = 2) with its peak at zero flow. One point uses a common rule: the head at zero flow is 1.33 × the head you enter, and the highest flow is 2 × the flow you enter, which again gives b = 2. A pump with no points entered adds no head at all. The curve is not stopped at zero, so asking a pump for more flow than its curve can deliver gives a negative head. The fix is a bigger pump or a smaller demand, not a different curve fit.
